title: Chapter 551
paragraphs: Chapter 551
Episode 145. Premonition (20)
The sky seemed as if it would crumble at any moment under the thunderous clash of two giants' power.
The outrageous explosions and shockwaves were turning Hairan's territory into a place where no one could live.

Beasts and creatures fled from the flames and the aftermath of shattered sword energy that stretched almost to the horizon, crying out in fear. Buildings melted, forests turned to ash, and water streams evaporated.
Who could believe that this was a fight of one man against the world's greatest?
Yet, the Sword Emperor City still stood.
The city maintained its form. Its high, thick walls hadn’t completely lost their function, and the enemies didn’t dare to storm through the broken city gates.
Even the inner city was in almost the same state as when Ron first regained consciousness and climbed the walls.
That place alone.
He couldn't let it break where his grandson was fighting alone against the white stone. The child couldn't win the stone and see a broken Sword Emperor City for the first time.
Ron defended the inner city with such determination.
Dry bloodstains filled the corners of his mouth and his hair was disheveled like a sick person's.
His emaciated upper body was filled with numerous scars that proved his life, along with fresh wounds, and his breath was rough.
Yet, his eyes, glaring at the enemy, sparkled with unwavering intensity, and his beloved sword, Rashid, continually emitted radiance, causing vibrations throughout the sky.
The guardian deity protecting Hairan.
That was the Sword Emperor.
"Kelliark Zipple, you. Your defeat is quite apparent... Seeing as you don’t talk of negotiation or run away, it seems you have some tricks up your sleeve. Isn’t it about time to pull them out?"
Despite his low voice, everyone on the battlefield could hear him.
The walls of Sword Emperor City were even lower, but the magicians and dragons of Zipple felt as if his voice was coming from a higher place in the sky.
As Ron took a step forward and swung his sword sideways, an invisible sword wind spread out, scattering Kelliark's grand spells.
In the meantime, the Emperor's sword, Bi-Gi Cheongong Ilseom, unfolded. The deep blue sword energy split the middle of the fleet, and Kelliark swung Huroti to offset most of it.
However, he looked strained. He coughed up a clot of blood, and his hand holding the staff was shaking.
Still using the same, no, even greater magical power.
Yet, Ron showed no sign of collapsing under his and the fleet's attacks. As time passed, one by one, the ships and dragons in Zipple's ranks began to crash.
'It's not an unexpected result... but it's a grim feeling.'
Is this to say that the gap is so large...?
Swallowing the bitter lump rising in his throat, Kelliark thought. The realm of Ron's abilities was beyond what he himself had experienced, so the result could only be bitter.

Just as Ron had fought to protect the Sword Emperor's Castle, Kelliark had also been unable to fully utilize his power, as he was busy ensuring that the shock did not transfer to the Magic Core Stone.
However, even taking that into account, Kelliark had to admit his complete defeat.
The Magic Core Stone had not yet been fully activated.

This was due to a lack of magical power. Kelliark was out of energy from dealing with the stronger Ron, and Octavia and the Spectre Army had infiltrated the Sword Emperor's Castle to secure the white stone, so only the magic of the remaining magicians and dragons was being used for the activation of the Magic Core Stone.
From beginning to end, everything had been out of his calculation.
The only relief was the fact that the opening of the Magic Core Stone was not far off.
And Ron also had a hunch about this.
'The fleet's attack is not as fierce as expected. Probably because they can't focus on the battle while trying to use the Magic Core Stone, as Jin predicted.'
Though he seemed relaxed, in fact, Ron was worried about the power of the Magic Core Stone.
Kelliark and Zipple did not realize it, but Ron was also getting tired.
Long illness and internal battles had definitely worn him out. The transcendent Muwi and the difference in class simply concealed that fact from his enemies.
Ron himself felt it keenly to his bones.
'If I only had one more month, no, even two weeks...'
He would have been able to fight in full condition.
If Kelliark pulls out a hidden card in his current state, can he really handle it?
If not, how much longer can he endure?
Ron could not answer this frustrating question. Just as Kelliark had never reached Ron's level, the Magic Core Stone was a completely unknown area to him.
However, Ron thought of his grandson.
'Fighting in this body, I now understand even more how much you must have suffered... Grandson, your grandfather has now come to understand the path you have walked.'
As his grandson had done, as he is still doing, he just had to keep fighting silently.
Grrrrrrrr...!
Kojak's cannon was turning golden. The cannon was fired following the same trajectory left by the Imperial Sword, Cheongongilseom.
Rashid, who had fallen like a bell, cut right through the center of the cannon. The cannon and the shards of sword light did not strike the ground, but disintegrated and disappeared in the air.
Such a huge force had collided with each other so many times that it was impossible to count.
Although they were outputting less than half of their usual firepower to open the Magic Core Stone, the attacks of other wizards and dragons, excluding Kelliark, were hardly noticeable.
In the midst of it all, only Ron and Kelliark's swords and magic enveloped the world.
Suddenly, a new force erupted in the middle of the battlefield.
In the middle of the sea, as if a huge whirlpool had spread, another power was cutting through the giants.
'Is it a power that started from the ground?'
'Can't be.'
Kelliark and Ron couldn't help but be captivated by this power.
Even while Octavia and the Spectral Army were tirelessly casting grand magic, their power had never reached the sky.
Moreover, the power that appeared to the giants was not magic of light or natural attributes, but was composed of a special deep blue flame and dark energy.
Jin and Misha's funeral pyre.
What surprised the giants was precisely that magic sword.
"Huhuh."
Unknowingly, Ron let out a hollow laugh. Such a tremendous power that even he, on the verge of spearheading, hadn't expected it would rise from the ground.
On the other hand, Kelliark could not laugh.
He was already stretched thin battling Ron, and the funeral pyre of Jin and Misha that stretched to the sky was now spreading a dark water-like energy towards Zipple's fleet.
The rune characters of Sarah, rewritten in spirit, began to leave a black glow like a tumor all over the fleet formation.
"Evade!"

Kelliark ordered them not to block it but to avoid it. Even before the order fell, those who had sensed the bad premonition immediately maneuvered to evade, but those who had no energy left from Ron's attack couldn't even properly see those small rune characters.
Kelliark hastily spread a shield towards them, but already the pyre of fire made up of black and blue was raging like crazy.
It was a form of fire that everyone saw for the first time in their lives.
Nobody knew that the name of this fire was the punishment for the sins committed by Zipple. This was all they could know.
This fire, which neither goes out nor disappears easily, started precisely from the 12th generation of Runcandel on the ground.
The spirit energy and genuine blue fire becoming a symbol of Jin was now a thing of the past.
Each of the magicians in the fleet are Zipple's elite. Instead of panicking, they were striving to somehow push out the funeral pyre, and therefore the progression of the fire was not very fast.
'Most of the power would have been directed at Octavia and the Spectral Army, but this is the aftermath?'
While it's true that Kelliark highly rated Jin, this was not a power he could unleash alone.
'It must be the result of Murakan, or Misha, one of them unleashing their full power to assist Jin. Jin Runcandel must have also used most of his power.'
The battle on the ground was as good as over.
If Octavia and the Spectral Army held out, the result would be Zipple's victory; otherwise, it would be the victory of the Gyeonghwangseong camp.
Kelliark couldn't be sure which side it was. The uniqueness of the power called spirit energy was not something that even such a magician could accurately gauge.
Moreover, Kelliark had another issue to worry about first.
"This is... Sarah... Runcandel's...!"
Feng Long, Salrion.
He was the dragon that proved the weakening of the power of the story, unconsciously muttering about the 'Ten Knights' when the second war first started.
Now, he was clearly feeling the nightmare of that era beyond his unconsciousness. He vividly remembered how many of his kin and magicians this terrible pyre of fire had killed...
The image of that monster-like Flame Emperor, Sarah Runcandel.
As Salrion was shaken, other dragons also began to show symptoms of convulsions.
The aftermath of the battle, the instinctive fear of the devil stone suppressed by the necklace, Salrion's voice, etc. were awakening the forgotten story from them.
"Escape, we must escape. Crraaack!"
Kelliark jabbed his sword, Huroti, into Salrion's back. It was better to make him faint so that he couldn't accelerate the damage to the power of the story.
Although the already insufficient power was dwindling further, it was not comparable to the aftermath of the story's power being damaged further.
'If we can just hold on a little longer, the opening of the devil stone will be completed.'
Within the next 30 minutes.
Kelliark raised his magic power once more. The front was full of Ron's swords.
Screeeeech-!
Octavia was hearing a sharp tinnitus ringing in her ears. It felt like someone was tearing and ripping apart her head.
'What... what happened...'
She had no feeling in her arms and legs.
She wasn't cut. Just that her body didn't listen due to the extreme shock of the funeral pyre, and for a moment Octavia recalled the moment when that black and blue flame engulfed her.
'Did I block it? What happened to them? Damn it, I can't remember.'
She couldn't remember well.
When she finally managed to move her hand and reflexively touch her face, Octavia realized that her left eye was gone.
It was an area that could not be recovered with light magic.
'Does this mean... I lost?'
Without any time to be dazed, someone flew next to her fallen body. A gray robe, one of the Spectral Army, who was already dead.
Only then was Octavia able to realize that the Spectral Army was fighting to protect her.
If it weren't for them, she would have died on the spot, not even able to open the one remaining eye.
